thread:
maria: Heads-up — Customer ACME reported duplicate charges after our SDK retried on 502s. They saw two successful charge events in their system. Request ID: req_abc123. Can someone advise quick mitigations?

alex: Which SDK & version? Do we have the request/response trace?

maria: SDK: sdk-js v2.0.0. Attached logs show a 502 returned from our edge, then the SDK retried and got a 200. Customer didn't set an Idempotency-Key.

ben: Ok — by default v2.0.0 will retry transient errors (502/503/504) up to 3 times for POSTs. That can cause duplicate side effects if the backend actually processed the first attempt before returning 502. Worth noting: our billing flow processes before returning final status in some failure modes.

sridhar: Important: Retry behavior + lack of idempotency key is the root cause here. Also check how we treat Retry-After header for 429s — separate but related. For 502s we do exponential backoff with full jitter (base 200ms, multiplier 2). If the first request reached the payment processor and was accepted, a retry will create another charge.

maria: Customer asked for repro steps so they can validate and confirm. Any simple way to reproduce locally?

alex: Repro approach: send same POST rapidly without Idempotency-Key, and simulate an intermediate network failure after backend side-effects are created but before the response is returned. Easiest is a proxy that drops/rewrites responses (or a small server that returns 502 after doing the work). Example curl flow to test:

```
# simulate non-idempotent POST (no Idempotency-Key)
curl -v -X POST https://staging.redwood.local/v1/charge \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount":100,"customer_id":"acct_123"}'
# Use a proxy that returns 502 for the first response after processing, then 200 on replay.
```

ben: Immediate mitigations to share with the customer: 1) set an Idempotency-Key header (UUID) on requests that create billed side effects, 2) downgrade SDK retry count to 0 or use config to not retry non-idempotent endpoints, 3) if they can't change client quickly, ask our Billing team to do a refund/dedupe while we investigate.

maria: Can you post exact config snippet I can give them?

ben: Sure — for JS SDK:

```
// Disable automatic retries for writes
const client = new Redwood({
  apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY,
  retry: { maxRetries: 0 }
});

// Or prefer idempotency
await client.request("POST", "/v1/charge", { body }, { headers: { "Idempotency-Key": uuidv4() } });
```

ben: For older SDKs where config isn't available, tell them to set Idempotency-Key header on every create call.

sridhar: Long term: we should change default in next patch to not retry non-idempotent POSTs unless an Idempotency-Key is present. We already have a branch for this. Release note: release-bot, any ETA?

release-bot: SDK v2.1.0 scheduled for canary tomorrow — default behavior will avoid retries on non-idempotent endpoints unless idempotency header is supplied. Patch PR: #789.

alex: Great. I'll open an internal incident for the customer case and tag billing + infra so we can check edge logs and dedupe. Maria, please include their timeline and request id.

maria: Will do. Also proposing we add server-side dedupe by transaction_id where available (defense in depth). Filing a doc + KB entry after we ship the SDK change.

sridhar: Agreed — KB should include: explanation of retries, idempotency guidance, sample configs across SDKs, repro steps, and how to request refunds. I'll take the PR for the KB.

maria: Thanks all — sending customer the immediate workaround (idempotency header + retry=0) and ETA for SDK patch.

alex: :thumbsup: follow-up: if anyone sees more customers hit this pattern, ping me and I'll prioritize a hotfix for the billing path to add stronger server-side protections.
